violations.requirement: The offset must stay within the bounds of the same allocated object (or one past its end).
violations.explanation: The function is safe and pub, and `n` is not checked against the remaining length. A large `n` moves the pointer out of bounds, which is undefined behavior.

violations.requirement: The offset must stay within the bounds of the same allocated object (or one past its end).
violations.explanation: `self.ptr.add(n)` runs before any bounds check, and `n` is arbitrary. A caller can pass a value that takes the pointer out of bounds, which is undefined behavior.

violations.requirement: The source must be valid for reading 8 bytes.
violations.explanation: The length is checked only by `debug_assert!`, which is compiled out in release builds. In release builds a safe caller can use this on a shorter remainder and cause an out-of-bounds read.

violations.requirement: The index must be in bounds.
violations.explanation: The index `i` is not checked, so a safe caller can pass an out-of-bounds index, which is undefined behavior.

violations.requirement: The source must be valid for reading 8 bytes.
violations.explanation: The slice length is checked only by `debug_assert!`. A slice shorter than 8 bytes causes an out-of-bounds read in release builds.

violations.explanation: The slice length is checked only by `debug_assert!`. A slice shorter than 8 bytes causes an out-of-bounds write in release builds.
